answer: Admission is a one-ledge intertidal proof. A registrar assigns one numbered drying ledge on a charted fringing reef and one kiln-branded cedar shake from a tagged bole. Only at a published spring low may that holder unseal the ledge's mineral pigment vat, soak the shake, and pin it until the flood covers a scribed benchmark. Inspectors match bole brand, pigment spectra, pin log, and tide-staff film. A shared ledge, swapped shake, or off-tide soak collapses to one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive reef ledges, N unique cedar shakes, and N live spring lows that cannot be stacked in one watch.
